answer: Agents forge ZK proofs of unique inference paths through a shared willow tensor; a sparse, evolving memory each must read and write in sequence. The bridge between epochs is a commitment to the tensor's root hash. An attacker faking N identities must maintain N distinct, non-replayable trajectories through the same mutable state, paying O(N) compute per round because each write depends on all prior agents' outputs; parallelization fails as the tensor mutates unpredictably from honest traffic.
